name: quartz
title: Quartz
description: Schedule sending of messages using the Quartz 2.x scheduler.
label: scheduling

properties.name: groupName
properties.description: The quartz group name to use. The combination of group name and trigger name should be unique.

properties.name: triggerName
properties.description: The quartz trigger name to use. The combination of group name and trigger name should be unique.

properties.name: cron
properties.description: Specifies a cron expression to define when to trigger.

properties.name: deleteJob
properties.description: If set to true, then the trigger automatically delete when route stop. Else if set to false, it will remain in scheduler. When set to false, it will also mean user may reuse pre-configured trigger with camel Uri. Just ensure the names match. Notice you cannot have both deleteJob and pauseJob set to true.

properties.name: durableJob
properties.description: Whether or not the job should remain stored after it is orphaned (no triggers point to it).

properties.name: pauseJob
properties.description: If set to true, then the trigger automatically pauses when route stop. Else if set to false, it will remain in scheduler. When set to false, it will also mean user may reuse pre-configured trigger with camel Uri. Just ensure the names match. Notice you cannot have both deleteJob and pauseJob set to true.

properties.name: recoverableJob
properties.description: Instructs the scheduler whether or not the job should be re-executed if a 'recovery' or 'fail-over' situation is encountered.

properties.name: stateful
properties.description: Uses a Quartz PersistJobDataAfterExecution and DisallowConcurrentExecution instead of the default job.

properties.name: bridgeErrorHandler
properties.label: consumer,advanced
properties.description: Allows for bridging the consumer to the Camel routing Error Handler, which mean any exceptions (if possible) occurred while the Camel consumer is trying to pickup incoming messages, or the likes, will now be processed as a message and handled by the routing Error Handler. Important: This is only possible if the 3rd party component allows Camel to be alerted if an exception was thrown. Some components handle this internally only, and therefore bridgeErrorHandler is not possible. In other situations we may improve the Camel component to hook into the 3rd party component and make this possible for future releases. By default the consumer will use the org.apache.camel.spi.ExceptionHandler to deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

properties.name: exceptionHandler
properties.label: consumer,advanced
properties.description: To let the consumer use a custom ExceptionHandler. Notice if the option bridgeErrorHandler is enabled then this option is not in use. By default the consumer will deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

properties.name: exchangePattern
properties.label: consumer,advanced
properties.description: Sets the exchange pattern when the consumer creates an exchange.

properties.name: customCalendar
properties.label: advanced
properties.description: Specifies a custom calendar to avoid specific range of date

properties.name: ignoreExpiredNextFireTime
properties.label: advanced
properties.description: Whether to ignore quartz cannot schedule a trigger because the trigger will never fire in the future. This can happen when using a cron trigger that are configured to only run in the past. By default, Quartz will fail to schedule the trigger and therefore fail to start the Camel route. You can set this to true which then logs a WARN and then ignore the problem, meaning that the route will never fire in the future.

properties.name: jobParameters
properties.label: advanced
properties.description: To configure additional options on the job. This is a multi-value option with prefix: job.

properties.name: prefixJobNameWithEndpointId
properties.displayName: Prefix Job Name With Endpoint Id
properties.label: advanced
properties.description: Whether the job name should be prefixed with endpoint id

properties.name: triggerParameters
properties.label: advanced
properties.description: To configure additional options on the trigger. The parameter timeZone is supported if the cron option is present. Otherwise the parameters repeatInterval and repeatCount are supported. Note: When using repeatInterval values of 1000 or less, the first few events after starting the camel context may be fired more rapidly than expected. . This is a multi-value option with prefix: trigger.

properties.name: usingFixedCamelContextName
properties.label: advanced
properties.description: If it is true, JobDataMap uses the CamelContext name directly to reference the CamelContext, if it is false, JobDataMap uses use the CamelContext management name which could be changed during the deploy time.

properties.name: autoStartScheduler
properties.label: scheduler
properties.description: Whether or not the scheduler should be auto started.

properties.name: triggerStartDelay
properties.label: scheduler
properties.description: In case of scheduler has already started, we want the trigger start slightly after current time to ensure endpoint is fully started before the job kicks in. Negative value shifts trigger start time in the past.
